message: In the 100mm polyurethane insulated (PU, closed-cell foam insulation) cold room (C1), Sam, the wall heat gain has risk of draining the solar budget in hot ambient. To check it I used conduction calculation (the 216 W wall gain estimate (E3)). I found 216 watts steady gain, about 5.2 kilowatt-hours per day at 35 kelvin lift, according to American Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air-Conditioning Engineers Handbook Refrigeration, 2022. I propose retain 100 millimeter PU with shaded roof and tight door seals. My position: not ready because night autonomy is not closed. In the direct current (DC, battery-driven) vapour-compression cooler (C1), Maya, the hot-loaded 1 tonne pull-down plus respiration has risk of one-day overload. To check it I used hand estimate (the 25 kilowatt-hour pull-down thermal energy (E1)). I found 25 kilowatt-hours thermal needing about 10 kilowatt-hours electric at Coefficient of Performance (COP, cooling divided by electricity) 2.5, according to Azzouz and co-workers solar refrigeration study, 2020. I propose staged intake plus evaporator fan for uniform 4-6C and ice-bank for peaks. My position: not ready because compressor size must match battery. In the cold room airflow and heat rejection path (C1), colleagues, the poor circulation and condensate has risk of hot spots and water pooling. To check it I used section layout (the cold room airflow section (E4)). I found forced-air loop over crates with outside condenser and drain holds uniformity with about 0.5 kilowatt cooling margin, according to Thompson postharvest handling guidance, 2008.
